description.narrative:
South African Institute for International Affairs (SAIIA) är en icke-statlig researchfokuserad tankesmedja som grundades 1934 med uppdraget att uppmuntra bredare och informerad medvetenhet, debatt och analys om internationella angelägenheter. Dess övergripande mål är att bidra till "ett välstyrt, fredligt, ekonomiskt hållbart och globalt engagerat Afrika".
För att uppnå detta bedriver institutet evidensbaserad policyforskning och engagerar nationella, regionala och internationella beslutsfattare i policyutformning. Institutet bygger också kapacitet hos nationella, regionala, kontinentala och icke-statliga aktörer för att de ska kunna engagera sig med respektive regeringar och afrikanska styrelseinstitutioner.
SAIIA har varit en Sida-partner sedan 2005. Sida fortsatte sitt samarbete med SAIIA genom att ge kärnstöd under strategiperioden 2016-2021. Det senaste kärnavtalet löper ut i december 2021. SAIIA har ansökt om fortsatt kärnstöd om totalt 37 miljoner kronor för att under perioden 2021-2025 genomföra sin verksamhet. Det ansökta årliga beloppet är 9.25 miljoner kronor. SAIIAs föreslagna program ligger väl i linje med Sveriges strategi för regionalt utvecklingssamarbete med Afrika söder om Sahara. Bidraget till denna insats bedöms strategiskt då det stärker pågående arbete med forskning på frågor som är aktuella förr den afrikanska kontinenten med syfte att informera och påverka beslutsfattare och på sikt bidra till ett Afrika präglat av god samhällsstyrning, fred och ekonomisk hållbarhet. Initiativet uppfyller Sidas bedömningskriterier.

The South African Institute for International Affairs (SAIIA) is a nongovernmental research-focused think tank established in 1934 with the mandate to encourage wider and informed awareness, debate and analysis on international affairs. Its overarching goal is to contribute to “a well-governed, peaceful, economically sustainable and globally engaged Africa”. To achieve this, the Institute conducts evidence-based policy research and engages national, regional and international policymakers on policy formulation. It also builds capacity of national, regional, continental and non-state actors to engage with respective governments and African governance institutions. Sida has since 2005 been a partner to the SAIIA. Sida continued its collaboration with SAIIA by providing core support during the strategy period 2016-2021. The most recent core agreement will come to an end in December 2021.
The overall goal of SAIIA is to contribute towards a well-governed, peaceful, economically sustainable and globally engaged Africa. Under this overall goal are four key result areas (KRA), each with their own expected outcomes, as follows: KRA 1. Contribute to strengthening governance, stability and accountability in Africa within the framework of key African and global governance mechanisms and initiatives with a specific focus on the APRM. KRA 2. Contribute towards enhanced climate change resilience and green economic development in Africa in a manner that enables a just transition. KRA 3. Contribute to sustainable and inclusive economic growth and resilience in Africa by pursuing greater economic integration through processes such as the AfCFTA and harnessing the opportunities offered by the Digital Economy in support of greater social inclusion. KRA 4. Contribute to building more effective African agency on new geopolitical and normative challenges in regional and multilateral fora, including the G20, as well as its external partnerships. The primary target group of SAIIA’s research outputs and engagements are African policymakers at the national, regional and continental levels. Other target groups include policy makers responsible for policymaking with an impact on Africa in international organisations such as the European Union, various UN bodies, the OECD, BRICS, the WTO and the G20. SAIIA also actively engages foreign governments that are involved in Africa such as European states, China, Brazil, the US, Russia and India. Finally, SAIIA targets the African media both as a dissemination channel of its research findings but also to build its capacity in areas within SAIIA's expertise.

description.narrative:
SAIIA reports on both the research and policy engagements including BRICS-related issues, green or critical minerals, just transition, climate change and COP 28 and the G20.
On the key results areas. A few of the many examples are reflected below:
Strategic Objective 1: To remain a leading research think tank on policy issues related to Africas governance, economic development, stability and voice in international affairs.
The four themes under this objective remain: 1) African governance, democracy and human rights in the digital age 2) Sustainable and just climate transition in Africa 3) African economic resilience and inclusion 4) African agency and international relations).
From July 2023 to June 2024, SAIIA commissioned 80 researchers from around the world. The use of SAIIAs international network to increase research output is assessed to be valuable in bolstering SAIIA's capacity and voice on key topics and themes. The amount of publications (70 research outputs), media appearances (135) and dissemination events (19) are assessed to be massive and on the whole the targets set in the research framework were exceeded.
SAIIAs governance agenda focuses on multi-stakeholder governance initiatives, particularly the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM), and human rights and governance in the digital age. During the reporting period, SAIIA continued its work on capacity building of African civil society with an aim to enhance states engagement with the APRM process. Through its APRM Popular Sensitisation Project, the Institute assisted a coalition of civil society organisations to compile and submit the Malawian APRM engagement that started in December 2022. SAIIA worked with the Malawi Economic Justice Network (MEJN) as its anchor partner in Malawi for the MAPS Project. The Malawi APRM Popular Sensitisation Project (MAPS) builds on five previous APS-projects in Namibia, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Botswana and Lesotho. During the reporting period, SAIIA begun scoping for the next country in the SAIIA APRM Popular Sensitisation Project:Tanzania and Angola. SAIIAs Memorandum of Agreement with the APRM was also renewed for a further three years during this reporting period.
On African governance and Human Rights in a Digital Age, SAIIA undertook research and organized events applying futures thinking around the use of civic tech in the Southern African region, building on SAIIAs growing body of work on democracy and technology. The partner organisation published a paper on the use of digital IDs and biometric technologies in East Africa. On Youth and Democracy: Under the umbrella of Sidas Democracy Hub activities, SAIIAs African Governance and Diplomacy Programme (AGDP) and the Youth@SAIIA programme hosted informal youth consultations on 26-27 March 2024 supported by the Embassy of Sweden in Pretoria on the value of regional civil society networks in promoting democratic governance and securing the future of democracy in the southern Africa region.
On Democracy and Governance future in Technology in SADC, SAIIAs Futures Programme (FP) engaged with key policy processes across the SADC to shape future governance landscapes through the lens of civic technology. The paper "Civic Tech in Southern Africa: Alternative Democracy and Governance Futures" by Professor Geci-Karuri Sebina and Amy Mutua, has informed regional and national policy discussions on reimagining democracy and governance in Africa.
SAIIA's work continue to significantly contribute to several national and regional climate policy processes re climate change and just transition. This includes continued support to the African Union Commission (AUC) on the African Union Climate Change and Resilient Development Strategy and Action Plan, and participation in high-level consultations convened by the AUC, SADC and UNFCCC (COP28). SAIIA has also contributed to several other policy processes in conjunction with COP28 for IGAD and priorities for African negotiators to take forward at COP28.
On green/critical minerals, SAIIA has built up a profile as a leading authority in this crucial field through research and policy engagements on the subject. SAIIAs team is working with African Minerals Development Centre (AMDC) to build up their capacity and develop an African Green Minerals Observatory digital platform that was launched in July 2024. The platform serves to inform and support policy dialogue on critical minerals governance and value chains in Africa.
SAIIA has been involved in developing mechanisms to assess the implementation of the AfCFTA, through for example its seat in steering committee on the Accelerated Industrial Development for Africa (AIDA)/AfCFTA Impact Assessment Guide as well as participating and contributing to workshops and consultation processes both on the continent and abroad on issues that impact Africas regional integration agenda.
SAIIA reports to have worked with sub-regional and continental bodies such as Southern African Development Community (SADC), the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD), the African Union and its agencies, SA government departments, universities and think tanks across the world.
SAIIA renewed its MOU with the APRM Secretariat, signed an MOU with the Brazilian Institute for Applied Economics (IPEA) with which it is collaborating on BRICS and G20 themes, and is discussing an MOU with the African Development Bank.
Strategic Objective 2: To Strengthen the financial and organisational sustainability of SAIIA
The audited overall financial results reflect a less favorable result for the reporting period from 1 July 2023/24 in comparison to the 2022/23 financial year. However, the results were better than the approved budget. The income from investments and the fair value adjustment positively impacted the deficit from the operational financial performance.
The Institute submitted a total of 25 research proposals and concept notes in the 2023/24 FY. It has so far received feedback on 24 proposals out of the 25 submitted, of which 13 were successful. This represents a success rate of 54% which is a drop compared to the 90% success rate recorded in 2022/23 FY.
However, the total Rand value of the successful proposals is just over R37 million which is very close to the rand value of the successful proposals for 2022/23 FY. It means that most of the successful proposals in this financial year have had larger budgets than the ones for the 2022/23 FY.
SAIIA reports that the drop in the success rate can be attributed to the fact that in this financial year some of the research programmes ventured into new research areas to expand their portfolios. For instance, some of the unsuccessful proposals were in areas such as artificial intelligence; information integrity and civic space; and global pandemic funding.
On governance and internal control, MASA Risk Advisory Services was appointed to conduct two internal audits to provide assurance that SAIIAs risk management, governance, and internal control processes are functioning effectively. The objective of the audits was to review internal financial controls and the human resources processes. Both reports were acceptable and highlighted no major concerns.
Strategic Objective 3: To improve our ability to influence policy and inclusive outcomes and deepen our collaboration across our diverse networks
For the period under review, Newsclip recorded 601 mentions of SAIIA across print, broadcast and online media. Media interest in SAIIA's expertise was high this year, with a total of 261 interview requests from journalists an uptick of 6% compared to the previous period. Of these, 200 requests were accepted by research staff and the chief executive. SAIIA has therefore successfully converted 77% of interview requests into media placements across a wide range of local and international outlets. Newsclips sentiment analysis for the reporting period showed a highly favourable view of SAIIA, with 84% of media coverage categorized as positive. This is assessed to reflect a strong public perception of SAIIA's work and messaging. The remaining 16% of coverage was neutral.
SAIIA's continue to be recognized as an advisor at high-level policy processes. To mention one of many examples, the Executive Director continues to serve on the UN High Level Advisory Board on Economic and Social Affairs, which advises the Under-Secretary-General for Economic and Social Affairs. She is also serving as a technical advisor on the AUDA-NEPAD Policy Bridge Tank. SAIIA continues to provide support to the Secretariat of APRM on its primary mandate. SAIIAs relationship with AUC gotten traction from directorates at the AU that were difficult to reach in the previous reporting period such as Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals (ETTIM). SAIIA also has continued to provide support to the Office of the Special Advisor on Africa to the UN Secretary General. Further, SAIIA has been appointed to be the T20 organising committee for the South African G20 presidency.
